recommendedFor: Hassabis viewing dossier for Dave (Oct 24) — the foundational long-form interview
summary: Recorded before ChatGPT, this is Hassabis's foundational long-form interview: he critiques the Turing Test, explains why games are AI's best proving ground, and ranges across simulation, consciousness, and AlphaFold. He also takes on fusion, quantum simulation, the origin of life, and the meaning of life itself. Partly dated now, but the clearest record of how he thought before the LLM era.
title: Demis Hassabis: DeepMind – AI, Superintelligence & the Future of Humanity (Lex Fridman Podcast #299)

recommendedFor: Hassabis viewing dossier for Dave (Oct 24) — dossier's #1 must-watch
summary: His post-Nobel return to Lex Fridman, and his most original recent interview. He lays out the 'learnable patterns in nature' conjecture from his Nobel lecture, touches on P vs NP, and covers Veo 3 and world models, AlphaEvolve, and simulating a whole organism. He puts AGI at a 50% chance by 2030 and weighs p(doom), consciousness, and quantum computation along the way.
title: Demis Hassabis: Future of AI, Simulating Reality, Physics and Video Games (Lex Fridman Podcast #475)

recommendedFor: Hassabis viewing dossier for Dave (Oct 24) — must-watch; the sharpest technical interview
summary: The most technically probing interview Hassabis has given. Dwarkesh cross-examines him on whether scaling is an art form, bolting AlphaZero-style search and planning onto LLMs, and weight security against rogue nations. They also get into governing superhuman AI and intelligence-explosion alignment, with harder follow-ups than he gets anywhere else.
title: Demis Hassabis — Scaling, superhuman AIs, AlphaZero atop LLMs, AlphaFold (Dwarkesh Podcast)

note: YouTube URL not verified in the Oct 24 pass — this links to the episode page. Content summary is from the episode's published agenda/transcript.
recommendedFor: Hassabis viewing dossier for Dave (Oct 24) — the business/operator angle
summary: The business-operator angle on Hassabis, with Harry Stebbings: what actually counts as AGI, the biggest bottlenecks, and whether scaling laws have hit their limits. He argues AGI is '10 times the Industrial Revolution at 10 times the speed,' explains why LLMs won't commoditize, and covers drug discovery timelines, regulation, jobs and inequality, and AI's energy demand.
title: Demis Hassabis: Why AGI is Bigger than the Industrial Revolution & Where Are The Bottlenecks in AI (20VC)

recommendedFor: Cataloged from the Hassabis dossier (Oct 24) — NOT recommended: period piece
summary: The series finale of DeepMind's own podcast, with Hannah Fry hosting: Hassabis makes his AGI pitch, touches on consciousness, and closes with a story about meeting Stephen Hawking. Charming, but its pre-ChatGPT framing makes it a period piece — Lex #299 covers the same era better. (A second Hassabis episode, 'The future of intelligence' from Dec 2025, also exists.)
title: The Promise of AI with Demis Hassabis (Google DeepMind: The Podcast)

recommendedFor: Cataloged from the Hassabis dossier (Oct 24) — NOT recommended: repeats the Sequoia set
summary: A fireside chat with Stanford President Jonathan Levin covering the 2010 founding pitch — 'solve intelligence, then everything else' — plus agents and AGI as the ultimate tool for science. It lands his line about 'standing in the foothills of the singularity.' Polished and quotable, but it largely repeats his Sequoia conversation, so the dossier marks it skip-as-rehash.
title: A Conversation with Demis Hassabis, Co-Founder and CEO of Google DeepMind (Stanford GSB)

recommendedFor: Hassabis viewing dossier for Dave (Oct 24) — must-watch; the 30-minute current position
summary: The tightest current statement of his position, in conversation with Sequoia's Konstantine Buhler. AGI by 2030 — year 16 of the 20-year plan he set in 2010 — drug discovery collapsing from ten years to days, and information as the fundamental substance of the universe. Despite the title, in the talk itself he anchors on the 2030 date rather than a 'three quarters' metric.
title: Demis Hassabis: We're Three Quarters of the Way to AGI (Sequoia AI Ascent 2026)

recommendedFor: Hassabis viewing dossier for Dave (Oct 24) — the founder-facing talk
summary: A founder-facing talk with Garry Tan on what's still missing for AGI: continual learning, long-horizon reasoning, and memory. He discusses 'fire-and-forget' agents and how to plan a deep-tech company on the assumption AGI lands mid-project, and teases news from Isomorphic Labs.
title: Demis Hassabis: Agents, AGI & The Next Big Scientific Breakthrough (Y Combinator)

recommendedFor: Hassabis viewing dossier for Dave (Oct 24) — the Hassabis vs Amodei contrast
summary: A Davos panel pairing Hassabis with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, moderated by The Economist's Zanny Minton Beddoes. The draw is the contrast: Amodei puts AGI at 1–2 years, Hassabis at 5–10 with '50% by end of decade' — and both say they'd prefer the slower timeline while citing the geopolitical prisoner's dilemma for not slowing down.
title: The Day After AGI — Hassabis vs Amodei (World Economic Forum, Davos)

note: Hassabis closes from ~1:44:28 — watch just the last ~15 minutes.
recommendedFor: Hassabis viewing dossier for Dave (Oct 24) — his keynote closing segment only
summary: Sundar Pichai hands Hassabis the closing slot of the Google I/O keynote — itself a signal of his standing. In the final stretch he frames AGI as the most profound technology ever invented and delivers the 'foothills of the singularity' line. Only the last ~15 minutes are his; the catalog recommends watching just that segment.
title: Google I/O '26 Keynote — Hassabis closing segment

note: Companion piece: the official Nobel interview (Dec 6, 2024, ~23m, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nkb4qEuxoJc) is the most personal/biographical of all his videos.
recommendedFor: Hassabis viewing dossier for Dave (Oct 24) — must-watch; his canonical science talk
summary: His canonical science talk, delivered in Stockholm: chess at age four, chess computers, games, AlphaGo, then AlphaFold, ending with AI as the tool for all of science. It's the source of the 'learnable patterns in nature' thesis he later expanded with Lex Fridman. The dossier pairs it with the 23-minute Nobel interview for the personal story.
title: Nobel Prize Lecture: Accelerating Scientific Discovery with AI

recommendedFor: Cataloged from the Hassabis dossier (Oct 24) — NOT recommended: covered deeper in Lex #475
summary: A polished conversation with Chris Anderson: AI as the fastest route to the big questions — reality, consciousness — plus AlphaFold's 200 million proteins, radical abundance, and a plea against a race dynamic. Beautifully produced, but every beat is covered with more depth and fresher detail in Lex #475, so it's a skip.
title: How AI Is Unlocking the Secrets of Nature and the Universe (TED2024)

recommendedFor: Hassabis viewing dossier for Dave (Oct 24) — the full-arc lecture
summary: A Cambridge alumnus's homecoming lecture tracing the full arc from his Cambridge CS days to DeepMind. It tells AlphaFold's CASP story, argues AI is cutting drug development from years to months, and makes the case for responsible development.
title: Accelerating Scientific Discovery with AI (Cambridge Lecture)

recommendedFor: Cataloged from the Hassabis dossier (Oct 24) — NOT recommended: historical baseline only
summary: A pre-ChatGPT, AlphaFold-era science lecture on using AI to accelerate discovery. Its value now is as a baseline: comparing his 2021 predictions against today's shows how far his timeline talk has moved. Historical interest only.
title: Using AI to Accelerate Scientific Discovery (Kendrew Lecture 2021)

recommendedFor: Cataloged from the Hassabis dossier (Oct 24) — NOT recommended: light explainer, superseded
summary: A short WIRED interview from DeepMind's science run — fusion plasma control, mathematics, and materials discoveries. Light and brief; the Nobel lecture is the definitive version of this material.
title: DeepMind's Demis Hassabis on Its Breakthrough Scientific Discoveries (WIRED)

recommendedFor: Cataloged from the Hassabis dossier (Oct 24) — NOT recommended: historical
summary: A short Bloomberg interview from the AlphaFold explainer era, on protein folding and the technological revolution it promised. Historical context only; superseded by the Nobel lecture.
title: Protein Folding & the Next Technological Revolution (Bloomberg)

recommendedFor: Hassabis viewing dossier for Dave (Oct 24) — must-watch; the 13-minute orientation
summary: Scott Pelley's second visit to DeepMind: post-Nobel Hassabis, Project Astra demos of an AI that sees and converses, Gemini learning to act, and robots following vague instructions. He puts AGI at five to ten years and talks about ending all disease within a decade. The best 13-minute orientation for a newcomer.
title: What's Next for AI at DeepMind, Google's Artificial Intelligence Lab (60 Minutes, April 2025)

recommendedFor: Hassabis viewing dossier for Dave (Oct 24) — companion to the DeepMind documentary
summary: A conversation with Hassabis and Derek Muller (Veritasium) recorded at the London Science Museum premiere of The Thinking Game, Greg Kohs's documentary about DeepMind's first decade from AlphaGo to AlphaFold. Hassabis is the film's central figure; this video is its verified YouTube companion. (His earlier 60 Minutes segment from April 2023 is superseded by the April 2025 one.)
title: The Thinking Game — Premiere Conversation with Hassabis & Veritasium
